evidence: AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase, ListOrdersByStatusUseCase and PlaceOrderUseCase all reach persistence only through the injected OrderRepository (findById, findByStatus, save).
GetStockLevelsUseCase reads products only through ProductRepository.findAll and maps them with toStockLevelDto from dto.ts.
dto.ts holds the only definitions of toOrderDto and toStockLevelDto, and every use case calls them.
ListOrdersByStatusUseCase validates the status by calling the shared assertOrderStatus from domain/OrderState; it does not re-implement the check.
PlaceOrderUseCase builds order lines through the domain factories OrderLine.create and new Order, and reserves stock through StockReservationService.reserve.
AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase share the guard `if (!order) throw new DomainError("not_found", ...)`. It is a routine lookup guard, not a duplicated domain invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module is one cohesive application layer for order and stock use cases. Each file is either a single use case or the shared DTO and mapper file.

Persistence goes only through the domain ports: OrderRepository, ProductRepository and StockReservationService. No file uses a database, ORM or query client directly.

Mapping is centralised. Every use case calls toOrderDto or toStockLevelDto from dto.ts instead of writing its own copy.

Order-status validation is a call to one shared definition: assertOrderStatus from the domain's OrderState.

AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase both repeat the same not-found guard after findById. This is the standard lookup pattern for a use case, not a duplicated business rule or invariant, so it does not count as a violation.

PlaceOrderUseCase checks customerId inline, and the domain Order constructor might check the same thing. That source is not provided, so the duplication cannot be confirmed.

No candidate flags were raised.
